work_items.title: Design baseline and migration inventory
work_items.objective: Finalize the accepted product specification, contracts, capability/evidence matrix, acceptance gates, and migration inventory before implementation work starts.
work_items.outcome: A reviewed design baseline and native implementation breakdown identify current CUDA consumers, runtime source identities, and cutover constraints.

assertions: The accepted product boundary and cross-system ownership are recorded
The explicit suspend-evict-run-restore-resume contract and failure behavior are recorded
The native plan lists DS-00 through DS-14 with dependencies
Live CUDA and Project Control resource consumers and runtime source identities are inventoried with evidence
Unimplemented and unqualified capabilities are labeled honestly

work_items.title: Core domain and adapter contracts
work_items.objective: Implement environment-neutral resource, lease, job, attempt, backend, handoff, policy, and adapter contracts with lifecycle validation.
work_items.outcome: Versioned core contracts enforce lifecycle and capability invariants without environment or transport imports.

assertions: Core contracts cover resources, requests, allocations, leases, jobs, attempts, schedules, events, managed backends, and handoffs
Transition validation rejects invalid lifecycle changes and stale fencing identities
Adapter capability declarations distinguish advisory, observational, and enforced behavior
Core imports no NVIDIA, CUDA, systemd, MCP, FrameShift, or Project Control implementation

work_items.title: Durable ledger and recovery journal
work_items.objective: Implement transactional SQLite persistence, migrations, idempotency, operation history, outboxes, artifacts, backup, and recovery fencing.
work_items.outcome: The service can durably record intent, reconcile external effects, and recover safely across daemon restart.

assertions: Schema migrations are versioned and transactional with tested backup/restore
Same idempotency key and request returns the existing operation while changed content conflicts
External actions have durable intent and stable operation identities before execution
Unknown observations remain unresolved and cannot trigger blind replay
Artifacts are indexed separately with bounded output and explicit retention controls

work_items.title: Allocation coordinator and policies
work_items.objective: Implement atomic resource bundles, topology/conflict constraints, shared and exclusive allocation, round-trip reservation, fairness, aging, and safe preemption validation.
work_items.outcome: Scheduling decisions are explainable policy proposals that the core validates before granting or reclaiming resources.

assertions: Multi-resource bundles are atomically granted in the ledger
Compatible shared GPU allocations are default and explicit whole-device exclusivity is enforced
Missing/stale required estimates block admission with an explanation
Default policy provides interactive preference, weighted fairness, aging, large-request starvation protection, and compatible background filling
Policy cannot exceed authority, capacity, interruption, or reclamation invariants
Accepted handoffs protect required execution and restoration capacity

work_items.title: Linux process supervision
work_items.objective: Implement transient systemd user service execution with stable attempt identity, supported cgroup limits, logging, cancellation, cleanup, and daemon restart reconciliation.
work_items.outcome: Processes are supervised and reconciled by durable attempt identity without blind relaunch.

assertions: Each attempt maps to a deterministic transient user unit and argument-vector invocation
Supported CPU, memory, and task controls are capability-reported and qualified
Cancellation and terminal cleanup account for the full contained process tree
A daemon restart can inspect running/completed attempts through stable unit identity
Ambiguous or missing records remain unknown instead of relaunching work

work_items.title: NVIDIA resource discovery and admission
work_items.objective: Implement GPU inventory, topology, memory/headroom estimates, opportunistic concurrency, whole-device exclusivity, quiescence, and profiling conflict domains.
work_items.outcome: NVIDIA resources expose explicit capabilities and policy inputs while accounting limits are distinguished from enforced controls.

assertions: Inventory and topology are host-qualified and refreshable
GPU concurrency is allowed for compatible requests by default
Explicit exclusivity blocks conflicting admissions until verified reclamation
Memory budgets are never represented as hardware enforcement without evidence
Profiling and quiescence requirements are represented as named shared conflict domains
Real qualification uses an isolated resource pool

work_items.title: Managed backend lifecycle adapter
work_items.objective: Implement registered managed-service profiles and llama.cpp launch, readiness, drain, eviction, restoration, and model residency accounting.
work_items.outcome: Backends can be operated by pinned configuration through journaled lifecycle actions with verifiable readiness and reclamation.

assertions: Backend identity pins launch configuration and version
Backend admission can close and attached consumers can be durably drained at a safe boundary
Stop/unload is issued only under an authorized explicit handoff
Resource reclamation and restored readiness are verified through adapter observations
Ordinary suspension leaves model weights resident unless a handoff explicitly authorizes eviction

work_items.title: Durable handoff coordinator
work_items.objective: Implement bounded request-suspend-evict-run-restore-resume orchestration, protected reservation, cancellation, failures, and phase recovery.
work_items.outcome: An accepted finite handoff is durable across client and daemon disconnects and settles only after execution, restoration, and delivery obligations are reconciled.

assertions: Handoff requires an explicit grant and fixed finite batch before acceptance
Protected reservation is feasible before stopping admissions or requesting drain
Drain timeout prevents eviction
Every phase persists intent before side effect and reconciles by stable operation identity
Results persist before delivery; failures preserve completed outputs
Restoration failure is visible and recoverable without rerunning completed jobs
Conflicting handoffs serialize and accepted batches cannot be extended

work_items.title: FrameShift continuation integration
work_items.objective: Add a minimal adapter for durable submission, safe-suspend acknowledgements, idempotent result delivery, and resumption at the pending logical tool boundary.
work_items.outcome: FrameShift continuations remain authoritative in FrameShift and receive durable handoff results after backend readiness.

assertions: Adapter exchanges continuation references without duplicating FrameShift internal frame representation
Shared backend consumers attach under an explicit standing drain contract
Suspension acknowledgements identify durable continuation and safe boundary
Result delivery is idempotent and resumes the pending tool boundary only after required backend readiness
Ordinary suspension does not unload model weights

work_items.title: Authenticated MCP, SDK, and CLI
work_items.objective: Expose versioned service operations through authenticated loopback HTTP MCP, a thin stdio bridge, typed Python SDK, and CLI.
work_items.outcome: All public surfaces share the daemon's authorization and application behavior.

assertions: Resource, lease, job, handoff, schedule, event, explanation, simulation, and health operations are discoverable
HTTP and stdio clients authenticate to one daemon authority
SDK, CLI, and MCP enforce the same scoped grants and idempotency behavior
Long operations return durable IDs and bounded waits do not cancel work
Command requests use argv, approved profiles/scopes, and host-managed secret references

work_items.title: Durable schedules, dependencies, and events
work_items.objective: Implement delayed and recurring schedules, nominal occurrence identity, overlap/misfire semantics, job-result dependencies, and authenticated events.
work_items.outcome: Scheduled and conditional work survives restart and produces deduplicated jobs under explicit calendar and overlap rules.

assertions: Intervals and IANA timezone calendar occurrences have durable nominal identities
Default misfire behavior coalesces to one pending run and default overlap is prevented
Alternative overlap/misfire modes are explicit and supported
Dependency cycles are rejected and dependency state refers to job results
Authenticated events are issuer-scoped and duplicate identities do not duplicate work

work_items.title: Explanations, evidence, and policy replay
work_items.objective: Implement inspection of queues, leases, ownership, operation histories, bounded artifacts, policy decisions, and side-effect-free replay.
work_items.outcome: Users can explain resource decisions and reconstruct operations without confusing simulations with execution evidence.

assertions: Decision views include policy version, reason, observation freshness, and relevant ownership
Execution evidence distinguishes ledger state, adapter observation, and enforced capability
Output bounds and truncation are explicit; destructive retention is policy-controlled
Replay performs no allocation, process, backend, or artifact side effects
Health reports unresolved and unavailable capacity honestly

work_items.title: Integrated qualification
work_items.objective: Pass independent lifecycle, crash, transport, concurrency, FrameShift handoff, security, and real GPU acceptance gates on an isolated resource pool.
work_items.outcome: First-release behavior and evidence limitations are independently reviewed and accepted before cutover.

assertions: All applicable acceptance cases have reproducible evidence and explicit disposition
Real GPU journey proves ordinary suspension keeps weights resident and explicit handoff reclaims then restores them
Crash/failure injection covers every durable handoff phase
Independent review confirms authorization, truthful capability claims, and no blind replay
Capability matrix reflects actual evidence and unresolved limitations

work_items.title: Consumer cutover and CUDA controller retirement
work_items.objective: Migrate active resource consumers, fence and retire the old CUDA allocation authority for migrated pools, and verify single-authority operation.
work_items.outcome: All migrated CUDA and narrow Project Control resource allocation/ownership-query routes use Device Scheduler; Project Control task and agent authority remains intact.

assertions: Active consumers and grants are inventoried and ownership is reconciled or transferred
Old allocator admissions are fenced before switching consumers
CUDA and narrow Project Control resource allocation/ownership-query paths use Device Scheduler
Project Control agent, task, workspace, coordination, Todo, and acceptance ownership is not transferred
Only one allocator is active for each pool in cutover and rollback
Relevant profiler, topology, quiescence, and isolation safeguards are preserved or replaced with qualified equivalents
Old controller/coordinator no longer grants resources to migrated pools

work_items.title: Final operational acceptance
work_items.objective: Verify deployment, documentation, recovery, authority ownership, evidence retention, and remaining capability limits after cutover.
work_items.outcome: The first release is accepted with an auditable operational state and explicit follow-on work for deferred capabilities.

assertions: Deployment and recovery runbooks match the qualified host behavior
Project Control and Device Scheduler responsibilities are documented and observed
Backups, evidence, logs, and artifact retention procedures are verified
Multi-host, hostile-tenant, arbitrary checkpoint, and Project Control agent lifecycle ownership remain explicit deferred boundaries
Final status reports completed evidence and unresolved limitations without overstating capability
